title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Milton Keynes

£30,000 - £35,000

Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity within a supportive and collaborative finance team?

We are recruiting for an Accounts Assistant to join a growing business in Milton Keynes. This is a varied role offering exposure to multiple areas of finance, making it ideal for someone who enjoys working as part of a small team and supporting wider accounting functions.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing the purchase ledger and processing supplier invoices
- Reconciling supplier statements and resolving account queries
- Assisting with month-end processes and reporting
- Maintaining accurate financial records and data integrity
- Supporting import/export accounting transactions
- Liaising with suppliers and internal stakeholders
- Assisting with ad hoc finance tasks and projects

About You
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant or Purchase Ledger role
- Strong understanding of accounts payable processes
- Experience using accounting software (Xero advantageous)
- High attention to detail and strong organisational skills
- Excellent communication skills
- A proactive team player who can support across multiple finance functions

Benefits
- Salary of £30,000 - £35,000 depending on experience
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Study support and career development opportunities
- Friendly and supportive working environment
- Excellent long-term progression opportunities

If you're looking for a varied Accounts Assistant position where you can develop your skills and become an integral part of a finance team, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Procurement Administrator
description:
Organisation: Cranfield University
Faculty or Department: Finance
Based at: Cranfield Campus, Cranfield, Bedfordshire
Hours of work: 37 hours per week, normally worked Monday to Friday. Flexible working will be considered.
Contract type: Permanent
Salary: Full time starting salary is normally in the range of £29,950 per annum.
Apply by: 22/09/2026

Role Description

We welcome applications from enthusiastic, well organised, team playing, previously office experienced people who have a positive mindset.

About the Role

To provide efficient and effective support to the procurement team, assisting with the administration involved around the processing of purchasing goods/services, their related financial activities for the University, A key part of the role is to support the Procurement Delivery Lead's, taking ownership of the central inboxes, categorizing emails accordingly, taking actions against emails when appropriate, setting up new suppliers as/and when needed.

About You

Must be enthusiastic, a team player, able to work independently to provide an efficient and effective support to the procurement team.

About Us

As a specialist postgraduate university, Cranfield's world-class expertise, large-scale facilities and unrivalled industry partnerships are creating leaders in technology and management globally. Learn more about Cranfield and our unique impact here .

Our Values and Commitments

Our shared, stated values help to define who we are and underpin everything we do: Ambition; Impact; Respect; and Community. Find out more here .

We aim to create and maintain a culture in which everyone can work and study together and realise their full potential. We are a Disability Confident Employer. We are committed to actively exploring flexible working options for each role and have been ranked in the Top 30 family friendly employers in the UK by the charity Working Families . Find out more about our key commitments to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Flexible Working here .

Working Arrangements

Collaborating and connecting are integral to so much of what we do. Our Working Arrangements Framework provides many staff with the opportunity to flexibly combine on-site and remote working, where job roles allow, balancing the needs of our community of staff, students, clients and partners.

How to apply

For an informal discussion about this opportunity, please contact Tracy Bates, Operational Procurement Delivery Manager (OPDM) on (T): or (E):

Please do not hesitate to contact us for further details on E: . Please quote reference number 5387.

Closing date for receipt of applications: 22 September 2026

Please note that we reserve the right to close this advert prior to the stated closing date should we receive sufficient numbers of applications. Therefore, we would encourage you to complete and submit your application as soon as possible.

title: Administrator (Learning & Development)
description:
Administrator (Learning & Development)

Location: Bedford (Fully Office-Based)
Salary: £25,000 - £28,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30am - 5:00pm
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

About the Role

We're looking for a proactive and organised Administrator to join our client's Learning and Development Team. You will provide admin support across learning, training and apprenticeship activities across the business.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative skills who is looking to build a career in Learning & Development. You'll work closely with the Learning & Development Advisor and People Services team, supporting training administration, compliance, reporting and a well-established apprenticeship programme of around 25 apprentices.

Key Responsibilities
- Coordinate training courses and learning activities.
- Maintain training records, learning systems and training matrices.
- Monitor mandatory training and compliance requirements.
- Manage learning and development enquiries.
- Support apprenticeship programmes and liaise with training providers.
- Produce reports and management information.
- Support onboarding and employee development initiatives.
- Maintain learning documentation, processes and records.

About You
- Previous administration experience, if within HR, Training or Learning & Development that would be an 'added bonus'
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work accurately.
- A genuine interest in learning, development and supporting people to grow.

Benefits
- Private Medical Insurance
- 5% Contributory Pension Scheme
- Electric Car Scheme
- Cycle to Work Scheme
- Opportunity to attend company events in London throughout the year
- Career development and progression opportunities
- Supportive and collaborative working environment

Apply Now

If you're looking for an opportunity to develop your career in Learning & Development and gain valuable experience within a growing People Team, we'd love to hear from you. This role offers exposure to a wide range of learning, development and people activities while supporting employees throughout their development journey.

Please be aware this advert will remain open until the vacancy has been filled. Interviews will take place throughout this period, therefore we encourage you to apply early to avoid disappointment.

Tate is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

Tate is committed to promoting equal opportunities. To ensure that every candidate has the best experience with us, we encourage you to let us know if there are any adjustments we can make during the application or interview process. Your comfort and accessibility are our priority, and we are here to support you every step of the way. Additionally, we value and respect your individuality, and we invite you to share your preferred pronouns in your application.

title: Underwriting Support Administrator
description:
Underwriting Support Administrator

Our client, a well-established financial mutual, is seeking a Underwriting Support Administratorto join their Operations team, reporting to the Operations Director. The role is responsible for collecting and processing medical and lifestyle information to generate one-off premiums for client care plans, preparing and sending quotes to Financial Advisers, processing applications, and providing ongoing administrative support for active plans.

This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-focused administrator from an insurance, financial services or care background who is confident handling sensitive information and enjoys varied, relationship-led work across advisers, clients and their families.

Key Responsibilities:
- Gather and verify medical, lifestyle and personal information to calculate one-off care plan premiums
- Input data into underwriting and premium calculation tools to generate accurate quotes
- Send quotes to Financial Advisers and respond promptly to queries
- Review completed acceptances for accuracy, following up on any outstanding information
- Maintain accurate records for active plans, including amendments, updates and annual existence checks
- Process death notifications sensitively, verifying documentation and updating records and payments accordingly
- Liaise with family representatives, care providers, Financial Advisers and internal teams
- Work closely with finance to ensure accurate billing, payments and record management
- Act as the main administrative point of contact for Financial Advisers, clients and their families

Requirements
- Strong administrative experience within insurance, financial services or a care setting
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Confident written and verbal communicator, able to convey information clearly to a range of audiences
- Comfortable handling sensitive medical and financial information confidentially
- Understanding of data protection and compliance requirements
- Proficient with IT systems and Microsoft Office
- Experience in underwriting administration or insurance quoting, or knowledge of care plans, is desirable

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a supportive, fully remote team, working across a varied and genuinely meaningful role that supports members and their families at important moments.

title: Accounts Assistant / Bookkeper
company: The GK Group Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Our client, is a small, friendly and well-established firm of Accountants based in Bedfordshire. They are now looking to recruit an Accounts Assistant / Bookkeeper to join its team.

Reporting to the owner, you will be responsible for:
- Maintaining client bookkeeping records using Xero
- Processing purchase invoices, bank transactions and bank reconciliations
- Preparing and filing VAT returns and MTD for Income Tax Returns
- Running payrolls and assisting with workplace pension administration
- Dealing with basic period end adjustments including prepayments and accruals
- Preparing year end working paper files for the accountants
- Assisting with management accounts and maintaining schedules
- Reviewing bookkeeping completed by clients and resolving discrepancies
- Assisting with onboarding new clients and setting up cloud accounting systems
- Supporting the preparation of quarterly and monthly management reporting packs
- Assisting clients with software queries and basic training
- Liaising with clients and HMRC on a regular basis to resolve queries
- Managing digital client records, document capture and filing systems

You should have 12-18 months plus experience within an accounting firm, have knowledge of Xero, be flexible in your approach and enjoy working in a small firm.

title: Receptionist
description: Do you have a friendly voice, a calm manner, and a passion for helping people? At Sharnbrook Surgery, our reception team is the first point of contact for our patients - they are that reassuring voice on the other end of the phone and the welcoming smile at the desk. Are you dependable, organised and able to juggle multiple tasks whilst remaining calm even on the busiest of days? Do you want to work for a close-knit, multidisciplinary team who support each other through the busy days and celebrate the wins together. An organisation who values open communication, flexible working, and a healthy work-life balance? Well this is what it is like to work for Sharnbrook Surgery! If you are reading this and think, this is me! This is the kind of organisation I would like to work for! Then we would welcome your application for the role of Receptionist. There is one part-time vacancy for 20hours per week. The working days are to be confirmed, however, please note that the successful candidate will be required to over 3 days, one 0800-1700, one 0930-1830 and one 1200-1600 per week. The successful candidate will demonstrate an ability to be flexible to do additional hours if required and offer flexibility for swaps etc. to support the needs of the service. Interviews will be held on Wednesday 21st October 2026. As Receptionist you will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a friendly, professional welcome both in person and over the phone. You will play a vital role in ensuring the smooth running of the practice through carrying out a wide range of administration duties including, but not limited to booking patient appointments, opening post, scanning health records, processing the registration of new patients and supporting both clinical and non-clinical colleagues. The role offers variety and opportunities to enhance existing skills and learn new ones. No two days will ever be the same. Primary Responsibilities The following are the core responsibilities of the Receptionist. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system i.e. make / cancel / rearrange appointments via the clinical system Processing of new and temporary registrations, patient discharges and all associated patient information as required ensuring accuracy and timely completion. Scan patient medical records, results and letters as required. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately. Signpost and support patients to the correct services as advised and/or as per pre-determined pathways. Ensure patient information is always up to date and accurate. Greet patients and visitors arriving at the reception desk, ensuring they have checked in. As appropriate ensure support is required in these tasks. Observe patients and visitors in the waiting room and alert an appropriate member of staff to any concerns or issues. This includes any wellbeing and security concerns. Ensure the waiting and reception areas are kept tidy and that information displayed is up to date. Updating noticeboards with regular health promotions. Ensure effective communications, regularly updating the Team Leader of any issues. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies. Always ensure confidentiality and professionalism with patients, visitors and colleagues. Assist in maintaining the safety of staff, patients and visitors. Always maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area, ensuring compliance with the Surgerys clear desk policy at the end of each working day. This includes wiping down workstation to maintain infection, prevention and control standards. Carry out any other duties as reasonably requested by colleagues. Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient and timely manner. Support colleagues throughout the surgery with general tasks as requested and appropriate Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to: Partake in audit as directed. Provide cross cover during planned and unplanned absences. Arrange and take minutes at meetings as required and appropriate. Raise orders for surgery consumables such as toners, hand towels etc. as instructed and required. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota. Support the OM with regular premises checks such as fire alarm testing and water testing as required. From time to time, individuals may be asked to take on tasks or projects outside their core responsibilities. We see this as an opportunity for individuals to broaden their skills, collaborate with different teams, and contribute to our shared success. These additional duties will always be reasonable, aligned with the individuals role, and designed to support both professional growth and the needs of the business.
